explain.say: A crawler, also called a spider, is a program that visits a page, follows every link to new pages, and keeps going, day and night. That is why its picture is a spider on a web. Why do you think links are so useful to it?

explain.say: Now look at index. Everything the crawler finds goes into the index, a giant list like the index at the back of a book. For each word it notes which pages use it. When you search, it looks in the index, not the whole web. Where else have you seen an index?

faq.a: A web crawler, or spider, is a program that visits web pages, reads them and follows their links to find more pages, so the search engine knows what is on the web.
asks: What is a spider in search engines?
How does Google find new pages?

faq.a: A search index is a huge organised list of words and the pages that contain them, like the index of a book. Searching the index is far faster than reading every page.

faq.q: How does a search engine decide the order?
faq.a: It ranks pages using many signals: how well the words match, how useful and trusted the page seems, how recent it is, and how many good pages link to it.
asks: Why do some results come first?

faq.q: Is the top result always true?
faq.a: No. Ranking measures how well a page matches and how popular it is, not whether every fact is correct. Check who wrote it and compare a few sources.
asks: Should I trust the first result?

faq.a: PageRank was an early idea by Google's founders, Larry Page and Sergey Brin, in 1998: a page is important if many important pages link to it, like votes.

facts: Google states that its search index contains hundreds of billions of web pages and is well over 100,000,000 gigabytes in size.
PageRank, which ranks pages by the links pointing to them, was described by Larry Page and Sergey Brin in 1998.

quiz.say: Why can a search engine answer in under a second?
quiz.show: Search is fast because the engine…

options.show: Reads the whole web each time
options.say: Reads the whole web each time

quiz.why: The crawling and indexing were done beforehand, so a search is a quick look-up.

wrong.1: Reading the whole web would take far too long.
wrong.2: It does not guess; it finds pages that match in its index.

options.show: Follows links to find and read pages
options.say: Follows links to find and read pages

quiz.why: Crawlers travel from link to link to discover pages for the index.

wrong.2: Crawlers read pages; they cannot delete other people's websites.
